set.typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. Applies to projects of five or more units (lowered from 20 by NS-3019, adopted April 19, 2022) that receive a discretionary density or land use increase. Rental projects: 15% low income, or 10% very low, or 5% extremely low, or a 10% mix (5% low, 3% very low, 2% extremely low). For-sale projects: 5% moderate income. In-lieu fee per habitable square foot of the entire project, tiered by size: $6.00 (5 to 9 units), $9.00 (10 to 14), $12.00 (15 to 19) and $15.00 (20 or more) (Sec. 41-1904(c)(1)). Effective January 1, 2026, a project of 20 or more units that elects the $15.00 fee must also sign an enforceable commitment that 30% of the construction workforce is a skilled and trained workforce (Public Contract Code 2601), with at least 35% of those work-hours under City local hire policies; the fee drops to $10.00 at 60% and $5.00 at 90% skilled and trained workforce. From November 16, 2021 through December 31, 2025 the workforce commitment was optional ($10.00 at 30% and $5.00 at 60%, with 20% local hire). The earlier NS-2994 amendment had cut the fee from $15 to $5 per square foot before the 2022 rewrite. Inclusionary Housing Fund receipts since inception: $31,147,483 (FY 2009-2020 $10,800,251; FY 20/21 $3,709,875; FY 21/22 $6,933,320; FY 22/23 $0; FY 23/24 $834,000; FY 24/25 $0; FY 25/26 $1,685,995 from the 408-unit Lowe Enterprises project at 2828 N. Main St.). Fund expenditures to date $20,558,250 for 224 units plus The Link interim shelter ($7,893,866); commitments $1,357,021. Only 35 on-site inclusionary units (25 ownership, 10 rental) have been built since 2011, so the ordinance functions mainly as a fee.
set.next_deadline: Applies at entitlement. The in-lieu fee amount is set at issuance of the first building permit and must be paid no later than the first occupancy approval for construction that adds net residential units (Sec. 41-1904(c)(2)). Fee schedule may be changed only by a five-vote Council supermajority. The Housing Element programs commit the City to periodic review of the threshold and fee.

New: since January 1, 2026 a 20+ unit project paying the $15.00 fee must commit 30% skilled and trained workforce (PCC 2601) with 35% local hire, with $10.00 at 60% and $5.00 at 90%; fee is set at first building permit and due by first occupancy approval. The skilled and trained workforce rule is not a prevailing wage rule, so prevailing_wage_trigger was left false.

Housing assets: real property $74,016,700 (statutory value) and loans and grants receivable $49,680,717, total $123,697,417. Prior year-end balances: $38,146,030 (FY 2020-21), $30,063,646, $18,112,239 and $15,956,650 (FY 2023-24). Attachments A and B list many Authority-owned sites (for example 554 S. West Ave., 309 W. Midway, 212 S. Beach Blvd. (Silver Moon), 428 S. Melrose, 883 S. Anaheim Blvd.) marked RFP pending or pending RFP process. Senior test 17% (231 of 1,382 assisted rental units, 2015-2024). Before dissolution the Agency's housing set-aside was $15,000,000 to $17,000,000 a year.

set.layering_notes: Anaheim's LMIHAF is active: FY 2024-25 deposits of $23.5 million and housing development spending of $21.4 million, mostly on extremely low income units, with $16.8 million unencumbered at June 30, 2025, plus a large land inventory with RFPs pending. The A-LHTF Guidelines say Trust funds may be transferred to the Housing Authority to combine with other sources for site acquisition. Housing successor funds are public funds under Labor Code 1720(b), but 1720(c)(4) excludes affordable units paid for solely from Low and Moderate Income Housing Fund money; other funds in the deal decide coverage (see prevailing_wage_basis). Housing Successor Agency page opened on anaheim.gov; FY 2024-25 report opened on anaheim.net.

set.typical_award_size: FY 2024-25 (SB 341 report): $3,164,557.92 deposited (including $3,000,000 of ERAF/SERAF loan repayments through the ROPS), $2,890,976.02 spent or encumbered, ending cash balance $3,092,947.34; total LMIHAF assets $24,689,712.27 including $9,870,187.74 of loans and grants receivable and $14,819,524.53 of real property. Development spending: $1,000,000 third installment plus $127,500 interest on the $8,550,000 purchase of the Civic Center Parcel (11390-11400 Stanford Avenue, northern portion of APN 090-154-57, exempt surplus land approved by HCD) for housing, and $1,550,000 encumbered for land acquisition (the remaining balance of the $8,550,000 price after installments of $3,000,000, $3,000,000 and $1,000,000). The Authority also committed $1,823,000 of LMIHAF (with an equal amount of federal funds) in FY 2023-24 to the 78-unit Orchard Grove rehabilitation and 55-year covenant restructuring, including 8 extremely low income units. Prior Housing Successor projects: Wesley Village (47 senior and family units) and Sycamore Court (78-unit substantial rehabilitation), both with 55-year covenants satisfying the Limon replacement housing judgments. Property at 11391 Acacia Parkway acquired 2019; 12291 Thackery Drive tied up in the New Age (Kam Sang) litigation.
